<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="By the end of this module, you should be able to:
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Apply California’s 5-Step CQI Process to prevention services.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Learn practical steps to integrate the 5-Step CQI Process into agency workflows.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="And develop strategies to overcome common CQI implementation barriers." /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Module 5 is broken down into four brief applications:
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Brief Application 1: Review of modules 1-4 and how to interpret fidelity and outcome metrics.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Brief Application 2: How to identify and define a problem from fidelity and outcome metrics and how to conduct a root cause analysis.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Brief Application 3: Developing, implementing, testing, and revising solutions.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Brief Application 4: Key implementation barriers and how to address them.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="In this session we will be covering Brief Application 3." /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Before we dive in, let's preview what you'll be able to do by the end of this module.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="By the end of this eLearning, you'll be able to describe what makes a solution fit the so-called "Goldilocks zone" — not too simple, not too complex.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="You'll be able to identify the key components of a strong implementation plan.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Explain what to monitor during implementation.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Describe how to test and revise a solution based on data.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="And recognize common errors in the evaluation and revision process.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Keep these objectives in mind as you work through the content — each one maps to a section of the module." /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="SinglePt5"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" Color="#000000" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="Let's orient ourselves within the CQI cycle before moving into the content.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="SinglePt5"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" Color="#000000" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="SinglePt5"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" Color="#000000" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="You're looking at the five-step CQI process. If you completed brief applications 1 and 2, you've already worked through Steps 1 and 2 — defining the problem and understanding root causes. This module picks up where that left off.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="SinglePt5"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" Color="#000000" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="SinglePt5"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" Color="#000000" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="Step 3 is about identifying a solution and planning how to implement it. Step 4 is implementation — actually putting the plan into action. And Step 5 is testing and revising — evaluating whether the solution is working and making adjustments based on what you learn.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="SinglePt5"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" Color="#000000" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="SinglePt5"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" Color="#000000" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="These three steps are where the CQI cycle produces real change. Let's look at each one." /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Remember the Cherry County HFA vignette from brief applications 1 and 2? We will use this to walk through each step in the 5-step CQI process.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="As a reminder, here is the problem statement: Between October 1 and December 31, 2024, the percentage of primary caregivers enrolled for at least three months in the Unity Center for Family Growth and Development's Healthy Families America program who were screened for depression within the required timeframe (within three months of enrollment or three months of delivery for those enrolled prenatally) was 20 percentage points below the target level.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="The root cause that was uncovered through the 5-whys: HFA caseworkers are not consistently screening caregivers for depression using the PHQ-9 or EPDS because they feel uncomfortable asking about depression. This discomfort stems from lack of training and practice." /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Step 3 is about identifying and planning a solution. Before the Cherry County team can choose a solution, they need three guiding principles.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="The first principle is that the solution must clearly follow from the root cause. If you did a thorough 5 Whys analysis in Step 2, your root cause should point directly toward a solution. A solution that doesn't match at least one root cause is unlikely to produce improvement— no matter how well it's implemented.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="The second principle is the Goldilocks zone — we'll dig into this more on the next slide, but the key idea is that your solution should be strong enough to actually change behavior, but not so complicated that it becomes impossible to implement reliably.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="The third principle is to avoid implementing multiple strategies at once. If you test two or three changes simultaneously, you won't know which one caused any improvement you see — or which one is responsible if things don't improve. Start with one targeted change." /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Let's spend a moment on the Goldilocks zone — because this concept is central to choosing an effective CQI solution.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="A solution that's too small or too weak is unlikely to create meaningful change. You put in effort, nothing shifts, and the team loses confidence in the process.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="On the other end, a solution that's too large or too complex creates its own problems. With too many components, it becomes difficult to implement all of them with fidelity. And if things do improve — or don't — you can't tell which piece of the solution made the difference.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="The Goldilocks zone is the middle ground: a solution that directly targets a root cause, is realistic given the team's capacity, and is simple enough that you can measure its effect clearly. As you review the three solutions on the next slides, ask yourself: which one sits in that Goldilocks zone for Cherry County?" /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Let’s say Cherry County has come up with three possible solutions. In your opinion, which best falls into the goldilocks zone.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Select the buttons to review each solution.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Solution 1: Skills-Based Training and Role-Play
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Let's look at the first option the Cherry County team considered. Solution 1 is a skills-based training and role-play. The plan is to hold a two-hour workshop for caseworkers that includes realistic role-plays using the PHQ-9 and EPDS screening questions. Caseworkers would receive scripting options — specific language they can use when bringing up the topic of depression. And there would be follow-up coaching sessions to reinforce what they learned. As you read through this solution, keep the root cause in mind: caseworkers feel uncomfortable asking caregivers about depression because of lack of experience. Ask yourself: does this solution directly address that root cause? Is it manageable as a single strategy? And is it something you could measure?
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Solution 2: Multi-Component Intervention
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="This option includes mandatory online training on depression for all caseworkers, new electronic workflows with automatic prompts to conduct screenings, parent educational materials on depression, and a depression screening guide distributed to all caseworkers. This solution covers a lot of ground. And on the surface, that might seem like a strength — more components means more chances to address the problem. But think carefully. How many moving parts does this have? Can you reliably implement all four components at the same time? And does it directly address the root cause — which is caseworker discomfort — or does it take a more indirect approach?
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Solution 3: Peer Shadowing and Mentorship
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="In this approach, caseworkers who feel less comfortable would be paired with more experienced peers. They'd observe their mentor conducting screenings over a period of two to four weeks, then gradually move toward conducting screenings independently with support. This is an appealing idea because it's grounded in real-world modeling — seeing someone else do it well can build confidence in a way that training alone sometimes can't. But consider: how would the team measure progress consistently across different mentors? What happens if mentor availability varies? Is this approach as straightforward to implement and evaluate as a structured workshop?You've now reviewed all three solutions. The next slide shows you the pros and cons side by side — then you'll be asked to choose." /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Here's a side-by-side comparison of all three solutions.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Solution 1 — the skills-based training — has a clear pro: it's a single, targeted, evidence-based strategy that directly builds the skill that's missing. The con is that it requires scheduling a dedicated workshop, which takes time and coordination.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Solution 2 — the multi-component intervention — addresses many aspects of the issue at once, which sounds appealing. But the con is significant: too many components makes it hard to implement effectively, and it may not actually fix the core issue — caseworkers' discomfort with asking about depression.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Solution 3 — peer shadowing — offers real-world modeling and gradual skill building. But progress is difficult to measure consistently across different mentor-mentee pairs.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Take a moment to review this table. We will check your learning on this at the end of this chapter." /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style LineSpacingRule="SinglePt5" /> <Span Text="Now that the team has chosen a solution, they need an implementation plan. An implementation plan is not just a to-do list. It answers five essential questions that will guide the team through implementation and help them evaluate results.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style LineSpacingRule="SinglePt5" /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style LineSpacingRule="SinglePt5" /> <Span Text="First: what is the improvement aim? This means stating specifically what outcome will improve, for whom, by how much, and by when. Vague aims lead to vague results.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style LineSpacingRule="SinglePt5" /> <Span Text="Second: what is the strategy to test? This should be one primary change — with an explanation of why this strategy fits the root cause.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style LineSpacingRule="SinglePt5" /> <Span Text="Third: what are the implementation details? Who does what, where, starting when, and what supports are needed?
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style LineSpacingRule="SinglePt5" /> <Span Text="Fourth: what is the data and learning plan? What data will be reviewed, how often, and who will interpret it?
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style LineSpacingRule="SinglePt5" /> <Span Text="And fifth: what are the success checks? How will you know the change is actually happening as intended?
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style LineSpacingRule="SinglePt5" /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style LineSpacingRule="SinglePt5" /> <Span Text="Finally — keep the first test small. Start with enough to learn, then scale up if results are positive." /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Let's see what Cherry County's implementation plan might look like in practice.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="The improvement aim is specific: by April 30, 2025, at least 70 percent of eligible primary caregivers at Unity Center will be screened for depression within the required timeframe — up from the current 60 percent.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="The strategy to test is the two-hour skills workshop with role-plays and scripting, followed by monthly coaching. The rationale is clear: it addresses discomfort directly.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="The implementation details: the CQI lead schedules the workshop in February. All twelve HFA caseworkers attend. Coaching is led by the clinical supervisor monthly.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="The data and learning plan: the CQI lead reviews depression screening rates monthly. Caseworkers share qualitative feedback at team meetings.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="And the success checks: the screening rate rises each month, caseworkers report increased confidence, and no eligible clients are missed.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Notice how each component is specific. That specificity is what makes this plan actionable and evaluable." /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" Color="#262626" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="Let’s check our learning before moving on.Select the button below to start." /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Now we move into Step 4 — Implementation. This is where the plan becomes action. The goal of implementation is not perfection. It's learning.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="The team is running a test to find out whether this solution works for this population in this context. To run a fair test, there are five things to keep in mind throughout implementation.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Stick to the plan as much as possible. The plan was designed to be tested — changing it mid-stream makes it impossible to interpret results.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Monitor progress regularly following the data and learning plan the team agreed to.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Communicate updates and challenges to all stakeholders — don't let surprises accumulate.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Watch for unexpected consequences. Sometimes a solution creates a new problem, or affects a group differently than anticipated.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="And document lessons learned — even when things go well. Knowing what worked and why is just as valuable as knowing what didn't." /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="We've reached Step 5 — Testing the Solution and Revising as Needed. This is where the team finds out whether the solution is actually working.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="The most important thing to understand about evaluation is that it should be planned in advance — not figured out after the fact. If you didn't establish a baseline before implementation, you have no starting point for comparison. If you didn't agree on a data review cadence, reviews will happen irregularly and be hard to interpret. The implementation plan the team created in Step 3 should have already answered these questions. The data and learning plan tells you what data to review, how often, and who will interpret it.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="The goal isn't to declare success or failure after one data point. It's to monitor a trend over time and make informed decisions about what to do next." /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Once the team has data, they may need to make adjustments. Here's how to do that well.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Adjustments should be clear, practical, and easy to implement. If you're changing course, everyone needs to understand what's changing and why.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Communicate changes to all stakeholders before implementing them — surprises erode trust and compliance.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="And here's a critical one: avoid making continuous adjustments. Every time you change something, you reset the clock on learning. Give each adjustment enough time to see whether it's working before making another change.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="A common pitfall is what might be called adjustment fatigue — a cycle of change where the team never stays with anything long enough to evaluate it. This feels productive but produces no learning. Before making any adjustment, ask: have we given this enough time? Have we communicated what we're doing to everyone involved?" /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Sometimes the data shows the solution isn't working, and the team isn't sure what to do next. This is exactly when to seek technical assistance. TA — technical assistance — is not a sign of failure. It's part of how CQI is designed to work.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Consider reaching out for TA when the solution has been implemented faithfully but the data shows no improvement after a reasonable period. Or when the team is unsure how to interpret the data or what adjustment to make. Or when new barriers have emerged that the team doesn't know how to address.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="External input can provide new strategies, validate next steps, or help the team see something they've been too close to notice. CQI is a collaborative process. Don't be shy about asking for help." /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" Color="#262626" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="Let’s check our learning before moving on.Select the button below to start." /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Question #2: Based on the scenario in the earlier slide, two of the four options identify real problems with the evaluation and revision process.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Think carefully about timing, about what belongs in an evaluation versus what's an overreach, and about whether the response builds or bypasses caseworker capacity. Select the two options that best identify the problems.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Option 1: The team reviewed data only one week after implementation — too soon to see meaningful change.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Option 2: The solution delivered (a workshop with roleplays followed by monthly coaching) was not the same as originally planned.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Option 3: The CQI lead's response — individually reviewing all cases —is not realistic.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Option 4: The CQI team should not have used the PHQ-9 or EPDS tools in the role-plays.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Select the button on the top right to review the scenario." /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Let's close with the key takeaways from this module.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="For Step 3: solutions should fall in the Goldilocks zone — targeted, manageable, and tied to the root cause. And don't start implementation without a plan that includes a specific measurable aim, clear implementation details, and a data and learning plan.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="For Step 4: stick to the implementation plan long enough to learn from it. Document everything.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="For Step 5: establish baselines before implementation begins. Review new data on a schedule, giving time for the solution to work. Give adjustments time to work as well. And when you're stuck, seek technical assistance.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="These principles apply across every CQI cycle, for every program type. The more consistently your team applies them, the stronger your results will be." /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Congratulations — you've completed Brief Application 3. You've now covered how to choose a solution in the Goldilocks zone, build a strong implementation plan, monitor implementation effectively, and test and revise your approach based on data.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Brief Application 4 picks up with a different kind of challenge: what happens when the process itself runs into obstacles. The next module covers three common CQI barriers — staff shortages, lack of buy-in, and time constraints — and the strategies that help teams navigate each one.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Thank you for your participation! You may now exit the course." /> </Block> </Content> </Document>
